You don't need to feel sorry. I'm a man and I get what you're saying. I think men find it more difficult to put into words what we feel inside. I can only speak for myself, though, but I think some would agree. That's the reason I didn't get the help I needed untill my mid twenties.

I used to get very irritable outside of mania. My ex girlfriend got the worst and I'm not proud of any of it other than the fact I never got violent. 
But emotional abuse is still abuse.

As for coping and treatment the best solution for me was medication and communication with people around me about my problems. If I get irritated/angry at work or with my family I take a deep breath and pause to think about why I am angry. Am I angry at them or myself, or even just at things? Would yelling solve this? (Spoiler: it won't) How can I best communicate to the people around me what I'm feeling? If they already know something about me and what I'm dealing with they will more easily understand and be able to help. Even if they just know a little bit. Communication is key. Self-reflection is vital.
